critic_notes.rationale: The expression matches the stated hypothesis and the level-minus-volatility cash-flow leg is a defensible conditioning variable, but the signal is essentially R&D-intensity (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis) crossed with a cash-flow quality/low-volatility screen, so novelty is modest and the true test is whether the interaction adds anything beyond the additive legs.

This is the most mechanical possible cross of two heavily published anomalies — R&D+advertising-to-sales and Novy-Marx gross-profits-to-assets — with no conditioning logic that a simple double sort on the two known factors would not already capture.

Dividing earnings by COALESCE'd intangibles plus goodwill creates a near-zero/zero denominator for the majority of firms, so the ratio explodes or drops out and the cross-sectional ranking will be driven by intangible-asset scarcity rather than the claimed earnings persistence on intangible capital.

Same denominator degeneracy problem (intan + 5-year R&D sum is zero for many firms, biasing coverage toward R&D-intensive names), and the second leg is simply a book-equity-minus-leverage ratio, making the composite a repackaging of intangible-capital turnover (Peters-Taylor/Eisfeldt-Papanikolaou) times low leverage.

Internally consistent (high intangible ramp × high cash-flow volatility/leverage → negative expected sign) and the fragility conditioning is a genuinely different angle from standard investment-growth anomalies, though GROWTH on a ratio whose base is often zero will generate outliers and the multiplicative form conflates low-growth firms with robust ones.

Both legs are published constructs (accumulated intangible/organization capital intensity and retained-earnings-to-book-equity à la Ball et al.), the product adds no new economic conditioning, and re/ceq is unstable for firms with small or negative book equity.

The quality leg is the standard Sloan (1996) accruals measure (ib − oancf scaled by assets) and the first leg is the same MA3 intangible-intensity term already used in two archive signals, so this is largely a known anomaly re-packaged as an interaction rather than a new mechanism.

Sign and construction are internally consistent and the cash-margin *trend* leg is genuinely different from the level/stability leg of the archived R&D Flywheel, though the R&D-capital-to-assets first leg is a well-known published anomaly and the one-period LAG adds essentially nothing.

The first leg is verbatim identical to two archived signals and the second leg (working capital minus leverage) is a generic financial-slack composite closely related to the already-tested "no debt build-up" and "retained funding" legs, making this a cosmetic recombination rather than a substantively different test.

The quality leg is a near-copy of the archived Flywheel's MA(oancf/at) − VOL(...) term, and the positive expected sign sits uncomfortably with the evidence that high goodwill/acquired-intangible intensity predicts *lower* returns, so the hypothesis and the first leg's natural direction conflict.

TS_COUNT(xrd,5) mostly proxies for reporting/data availability and is collinear with the R&D-intensity term it is summed with, and the remaining structure (R&D intensity × profitability level minus volatility) is a near-duplicate of the archived Stable Cash R&D Flywheel with ni substituted for oancf.

This is a well-diagnosed repair of the failed "Fragile Intangible Ramp" — replacing the degenerate GROWTH-from-near-zero base with a smoothed level change and swapping the fragility leg for a profitability trend — and the expression's direction correctly matches the stated negative sign.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archive's "Lagged R&D Cash Harvest" (same two legs, with the deflator switched from assets to sales and windows nudged from 3 to 5), so it tests no new economic mechanism and its first leg is essentially the well-known R&D-to-sales intensity anomaly.

The advertising-stock-only leg is genuinely new relative to the archive's xrd+xad blends and the mean-minus-vol cash-margin quality leg is coherently signed, though COALESCE(xad,0) creates a large mass point of non-reporters that will make the first-leg rank partly a reporting-status dummy and the advertising level effect itself is close to published brand-capital results.

The xrd/(xrd+dp) investment-mix ratio is a genuinely different construct from the intensity ratios already tested and is well matched to the stated hypothesis, but the second leg is little more than a cash-margin profitability sort (a known anomaly) and the mix ratio is undefined/degenerate when both xrd and dp are near zero.

Structurally this is the archive's top-performing "Stable Cash R&D Flywheel" with ib substituted for oancf, and it is internally inconsistent/mechanical: R&D is added into the level numerator but excluded from the volatility term, so high-R&D firms are mechanically pushed up on both legs and the interaction double-counts the same variable.

A defensible diagnosis-driven repair of the failed static-goodwill signal (level to increment, total liabilities to interest-bearing debt) with signs consistent throughout, though rising goodwill plus rising debt is largely a repackaging of the asset-growth/acquirer-underperformance anomaly and DELTA(gdwl) is zero for most firm-months.

R&D contraction conditioned on prior research commitment and deteriorating cash generation is a substantively new mechanism in this archive (previous R&D-decline tests were absent) and the triple rank product is correctly signed, with the main risk being noise and compressed dispersion from multiplying three ranks.

This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Knowledge Depreciation Mix" (identical first leg, second leg merely swaps MA for the TREND already used in "Lagged R&D Cash Harvest"), so it recombines two evaluated signals without adding a new mechanism.

Internally consistent and a defensible reframing of the failed intangible-ramp family (ramp rewarded only when cash conversion improves and leverage does not rise), though it overlaps materially with "Knowledge Spend Turnover Discipline" apart from level-vs-change and sales-productivity-vs-cash-margin substitutions.

The TS_MIN R&D floor leg is lifted directly from "Minimum R&D Earnings Persistence," but the replacement quality leg (cash-flow trend minus earnings trend) is a substantively different accrual-quality condition rather than a cosmetic tweak — with the caveat that this leg is close to a trend version of the well-known accruals anomaly.

Sign logic is coherent and the working-capital-scaling condition is a genuinely different conditioner than prior legs, but note it takes the opposite view of net working capital from the archived "Liquidity-Strained R&D Expansion" (which treated falling NWC as the bad state), so the proposal should acknowledge that it is implicitly betting on the accruals interpretation.

Both legs are near-direct rediscoveries of published anomalies (goodwill/asset growth and Sloan accruals expressed as earnings-minus-cash-flow), and it is the third goodwill-deterioration variant after two archived versions already returned t-stats near zero.

The advertising-versus-R&D composition shift conditioned on cash-margin decay is a genuinely new construct with a consistent expected sign, but COALESCE(xad,0) will zero out the advertising delta for the majority of firms that never report xad, collapsing the first leg into a pure negative-ΔR&D term for most of the cross-section — worth restricting to firms with non-missing xad.

This is the archived "Internal Innovation Over Acquisition" expression verbatim with RANK swapped for IND_RANK — a legitimate robustness check but a cosmetic re-parameterization rather than a new mechanism, and it should be run as a diagnostic on the existing signal, not proposed as a distinct signal.

Internally consistent and economically coherent, though it is a recombination that pairs the archived winner's organic-vs-acquired leg with a quality leg that is arithmetically near-identical to the already-tested (and weak-alpha) "Self-Funded Knowledge Surplus" cash-surplus term, so the incremental information content is modest.

The quality leg (oancf − ib) is a direct restatement of the published Sloan accruals anomaly, and the pairing with a TS_MIN knowledge-spend floor closely duplicates the archived "Cash Earnings R&D Floor" (cash-vs-earnings gap conditioned on a minimum R&D commitment) in levels rather than trends.

The MIN(xrd/sale, xad/sale) construct is genuinely novel but, because COALESCE fills missing xad with zero, the leg collapses to a large tied mass at zero and effectively becomes a dual-reporter indicator, and subtracting VOL(ib/at) from MA(oancf/sale) mixes incompatible scalings so the quality leg's composition is not what the hypothesis states.

Coherent and consistently signed, extending the archived Knowledge Depreciation Mix to brand spending with a genuinely different retained-earnings-minus-earnings-volatility quality leg, though the two legs' overlap with prior tests and the volatility term's likely dominance in the subtraction keep the expected novelty limited.

The "rising debt plus deteriorating operating cash flow" composite has already failed three times in the archive (Goodwill Cashflow Deterioration, Debt-Funded Goodwill Decay, R&D Abandonment Cash Squeeze, all with null or wrong-signed slopes), and the first leg is largely a sign-flipped restatement of the archived winner's organic-vs-acquired term, so this is a low-prior repackaging rather than a new mechanism.

This is a mechanical recombination of two already-tested legs — the identical organic-minus-acquired intangible leg from "Internal Innovation Over Acquisition"/"Cash Surplus Organic Intangibles" and the level-minus-volatility earnings leg already used in "Earnings-Stable Intangible Build" (only the MA window changes from 3 to 5) — so it adds no new economic mechanism.

Both legs are copied verbatim from the archive ("Organic Formation Cash Share" leg 1 and "Internal Innovation Over Acquisition" leg 2), making this a pure cross-pairing of previously evaluated components rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The reinvestment-mix leg is essentially identical to "Intangible Reinvestment Retention" leg 1 (and a close cousin of "Knowledge Depreciation Mix") while the cash-after-intangibles leg is verbatim from "Cash Surplus Organic Intangibles," so the expected result is a predictable rehash of two already-strong tested legs.

The TS_MIN R&D-floor leg is reused from prior tests, but pairing it with cash-flow-to-current-liabilities introduces a genuinely untested near-term liquidity-coverage dimension (rather than another oancf/at or oancf/sale trend variant), and the construction is clean and sign-coherent, albeit simple and close to a known R&D-intensity × profitability interaction.

The quality leg subtracts dlc/act from MA(oancf/sale) — two ratios with unrelated denominators and very different cross-sectional dispersion — so the leg is not the stated "cash conversion net of short-debt burden" but will be mechanically dominated by whichever component has larger scale, an internally inconsistent construction that a SUMRANK of the two would fix.

The first leg is identical to the archived "Dual-Channel Cash Margin" (same ~3% coverage risk), and the stated motivation is factually wrong — the prior version already used raw xad without COALESCE and in fact delivered fmb 3.01 / ls_talpha 2.51 — so this is a cosmetic quality-leg swap justified by a misdiagnosed failure mode.

This is a mechanical leg-swap between two already-tested archive winners (the xrd/(xrd+dp) mix leg of "Knowledge Depreciation Mix" and the identical MA(oancf/lct,3) leg of "R&D Floor Liability Coverage"), so it tests no new mechanism and will be highly collinear with both predecessors.

The earnings-floor conditioner is a genuinely different quality leg than the archive's cash-to-current-assets version and plausibly diagnoses why "Intangible Adjusted Sales Efficiency" had a decent slope but negligible alpha, though the knowledge-stock adjustment to the denominator is nearly monotone with plain sale/at and TS_MIN(ib/at,5) risks being a repackaged profitability-persistence proxy.

The intangible leg is identical to "Ranked Short-Debt Knowledge Cushion" and only the deflators in the quality leg change (sale→lct, act→lct), making this a cosmetic variant; worse, the stated motivation ("avoiding incompatible raw-ratio subtraction") misdescribes the predecessor, which already used SUMRANK.

Both legs are deflated by current liabilities, so low-lct firms score high on both and the product largely double-counts a single balance-sheet characteristic rather than creating a true intangible×quality interaction; it is otherwise a deflator swap on "Lagged R&D Cash Harvest."

This re-runs the failed "R&D Abandonment Cash Squeeze" triple-product structure with a deflator/level-versus-trend swap in the stress leg, and the NEG(MA(oancf/lct)) term alone is essentially a low-profitability/distress proxy that would mechanically deliver the negative sign without evidencing the R&D-abandonment channel.

It is the archive's already-well-tested "spending floor × high-and-stable profitability" template with ib/lct substituted for ib/at or oancf/at, and the MA-minus-VOL construction on a ratio with an unbounded, highly skewed denominator makes the level/volatility weighting arbitrary.

This is a cosmetic recombination of archived legs — the identical TS_MIN knowledge-floor leg from "Ranked Short-Debt Knowledge Cushion"/"Knowledge Floor Maturity Quality" paired with a cash-coverage-of-current-liabilities leg already tested in "R&D Floor Liability Coverage", with the only innovation being adding knowledge spend to the coverage denominator.

It is a genuine, diagnostically motivated extension of "Lagged R&D Cash Harvest" that directly tests the harvest-vs-abandonment interpretation implied by the archive's sign-contradicting "R&D Cut Liquidity Tightening" result, though the added Δ-R&D leg makes it only a moderate step beyond existing signals.

Leg one is functionally the same organic-formation share as the archived "Organic Formation Cash Share" (scale-invariance makes the at-normalization difference immaterial), and leg two merely swaps the cash-margin quality leg for the liability-coverage leg proposed elsewhere in this same batch — a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

This is the archived "Intangible-Adjusted Sales Earnings Floor" with a single numerator substitution (sale → oancf); the cash-productivity framing is defensible but the change is one-variable and does not address why that archived signal produced only a 2.3% alpha.

Leg one replicates the knowledge/(knowledge+dp) reinvestment-mix ratio already used in "Knowledge Depreciation Mix" and "Intangible Reinvestment Retention", and leg two is the same cash-versus-obligations coverage construct proposed elsewhere in this batch, so the signal is a re-shuffle of tested components.

Both legs are lifted intact from the archive — the intangible-adjusted sales-productivity trend from "Intangible-Adjusted Sales Earnings Floor" and the oancf/lct plus short-debt-concentration quality block from "R&D Floor Liability Coverage" and "Knowledge Floor Maturity Quality" — making this a mechanical crossover with no new economic content and ~7% coverage.

This is the archived "R&D Capital Cash Return" (fmb 1.82, alpha 5.3%, t 4.41) with a TS_MIN(ib/at) earnings-floor term bolted on via SUMRANK — a cosmetic dilution of an existing signal rather than a new mechanism, and the added leg duplicates the earnings-floor screen already tested in "Cash Earnings R&D Floor."

This is a mechanical merge of two already-evaluated signals ("R&D Harvest Cash Conversion" and "Brand Harvest Cash Conversion") obtained only by replacing xrd with xrd+xad and shifting the accumulation window, with no new economic content.

It extends the archived brand-harvest construct with a genuinely new gross-margin/pricing-power channel that directly tests the stated mechanism, though the two trend terms in the quality leg are highly collinear and the base construct was already weak (t 1.86), so the incremental gain is uncertain.

It replaces the level of organic knowledge spend — the leg that carried the archive's successful organic-vs-acquired signals — with a 3-year trend, the exact "intangible ramp/growth" formulation that has failed repeatedly in this archive (Fragile Intangible Ramp, Intangible Overbuild, Cash-Funded Research Ramp, Working-Capital-Light Knowledge Growth), and additionally subtracts a 3-year slope from a 1-year change with inconsistent scaling.

This is "R&D Floor Liability Coverage" with the strong level term MA(oancf/lct) swapped for a trend (already tested weaker in "Cash-Covered R&D Consistency," t 1.49) plus a NEG(DELTA(lct/act)) leg whose assumed direction is contradicted by the archived "R&D Cut Liquidity Tightening" result, making it a likely degradation dressed as a refinement.

The double time-series-minimum construction is an internally consistent and economically coherent durability test that differs substantively from the MA-based cash-surplus versions already tried, though it remains a fairly incremental recombination of legs whose individual value is largely known.

The R&D-stock leg is identical to the archived "R&D Capital Cash Return" and the level-minus-volatility quality leg is lifted verbatim from "Stable Cash R&D Flywheel," so this is a pairwise recombination of two existing legs (a defensible state-vs-trend switch, but marginal novelty over an already-strong archive result with talpha 4.4).

The intangible leg is character-for-character the archived "Organic Intensity Acquisition Load" leg and the liquidity leg is the already-tested SUMRANK(act/lct, oancf-coverage) block from "Research Floor Current Liquidity," making this a cosmetic quality-leg swap rather than a new mechanism.

This is a near-duplicate of "Persistent Knowledge Cash Surplus" (drop xad, change the surplus denominator from at to lct) crossed with "R&D Floor Liability Coverage," so both legs are already in the archive and the change is a scaling choice, not an economic distinction.

It reuses the archive's best-performing organic-versus-acquired leg but pairs it with a genuinely new element—cash return trend on a knowledge-capitalized asset base—plus a retained-earnings funding condition, giving a coherent monetization test, though the three-way conditioning adds overfitting risk and only incremental distance from "Cash Surplus Organic Intangibles."

This is the archived "Innovation Commercialization Handoff" (fmb 1.94, talpha 1.61) with a gross-margin trend appended to the cash-margin trend, i.e., exactly the cosmetic variant of a weak prior signal that the objective warns against, and the gross-margin leg is itself already tested in "Brand Pricing Power Harvest."

Both legs are archived verbatim ("R&D Harvest Cash Conversion" plus the SUB(TREND(oancf/at), TREND(ib/at)) block from "Cash Earnings R&D Floor"), and the new conditioning term is essentially a declining-accruals proxy, so the proposal largely re-tests the Sloan accruals anomaly inside an already-evaluated harvest construction.
